quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 16 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a result of riding in cold weather for long periods?
questions.explanation: Long rides in cold weather can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from the cold.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview mirror?
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust both mirrors before starting your motorcycle. Position them so you can see the lane behind you and the lane next to you.

questions.question: In general, riders should:

options.text: Always stay in the same lane position
Change lane positions frequently to stay alert
Choose a lane position that gives them the most space around them
Never use the center lane position

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives them the most space around them
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions are always changing. Pick the lane position that gives you the most space and makes you most visible to other drivers.

questions.question: A helmet should NOT:

options.text: Have been worn in an accident

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been worn in an accident
questions.explanation: A good helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards, fits snugly, and has no visible damage. If a helmet was worn during a crash, replace it.

questions.question: If you shift into a lower gear while riding too fast, what happens?

options.text: The motorcycle will jerk forward and the rear tire may skid
The motorcycle will accelerate too quickly
The front tire will likely skid
The engine will make a loud noise

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle will jerk forward and the rear tire may skid
questions.explanation: If you are riding too fast when shifting to a lower gear, the motorcycle will jerk forward and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: A person is considered legally intoxicated at a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is considered legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to operate a motorcycle while intoxicated.

questions.question: An experienced rider:

options.text: Changes lane positions as road and traffic conditions change
Stays in one part of the lane at all times
Weaves within the lane to be more visible
Only travels on the oily part of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes lane positions as road and traffic conditions change
questions.explanation: A motorcyclist has three lane position options. Choose the safest position based on current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When riding at night, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Use your high beam light when possible

questions.explanation: When riding at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Use your high beam, except when meeting or following another vehicle.

questions.question: Which colors make riders most visible?
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to make yourself visible to other drivers.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT increase rider visibility?

options.text: Using your headlight at all times

questions.explanation: To increase visibility, wear bright clothing with reflective materials, use your headlight at all times, and use your signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is usually a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers about traffic rules like speed limits. These signs are rectangular, white, and have black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop until the animal loses interest.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Dogs often chase motorcycles. If a dog chases you, slow down and approach it carefully. Then speed up and ride away from it.

questions.question: Riding next to another vehicle is unsafe because:

options.text: You may have a difficult time getting to a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It prevents other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. You may be in a spot the driver cannot see. The driver might change lanes and hit you without knowing you are there. The vehicle also blocks your way to escape if a problem occurs.

questions.question: Riding next to another vehicle:

options.text: Can place you in the driver's blind spot.
Is better than riding behind the other vehicle.
Is safe because it limits your escape routes.
Should only be done during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can place you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride next to another vehicle. You may be in the driver's blind spot. If the driver does not see you, they may enter your lane. Riding next to a vehicle also blocks your way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: A helmet will not protect you well if it:
questions.explanation: A helmet must be certified by the Department of Transportation (DOT) and fit snugly to give the best protection. It should have no damage like cracks, loose padding, or torn straps.

questions.question: Research shows that motorcycles with headlights on during the day are:

options.text: Not as easy to see as other vehicles.
More visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
Less safe than with headlights off.

questions.correctAnswerText: More visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times when riding. During the day, a motorcycle with its headlight on is twice as likely to be seen by other drivers.
